PAGE 1: SOLUTES AND SOLVENT

Grade 8 · Integrated Science · Topic 2.2: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell

▸ Today’s idea

• Solutes and solvent — read, see the example, then do Your turn.

▸ Learn

Today we study: Solutes and solvent.

When a solid is dissolved in a liquid, we get a solution formed. The solid that dissolves in this solution is called the solute.

• The liquid that dissolves the solid is known as the solvent.
• Sugar and salt are examples of substances (solutes) that are soluble in water (solvent)

▸ Worked example

• Ice → water → steam: change of state (physical) — substance is still water.
• Burning paper: new substances form (chemical change) — you cannot get the paper back.

PAGE 2: CONCENTRATION

Grade 8 · Integrated Science · Topic 2.2: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell

▸ Today’s idea

• Concentration — read, see the example, then do Your turn.

▸ Learn

Today we study: Concentration.

When there are more solute molecules compared to solvent molecules, a solution is said to be concentrated. When there are more solvent molecules compared to solute molecules, then the solution is said to be dilute.

• DIFFUSION. An experiment to demonstrate diffusion in liquids. Requirements: A beaker. DIFFUSION. An experiment to demonstrate diffusion in liquids. Requirements: A beaker.
• An experiment to demonstrate diffusion in liquids.

Today we study: DIFFUSION.

An experiment to demonstrate diffusion in liquids. What you do / what happens:

1. Pour some water in a beaker.
2. Put a drop of the dye or ink in the water.
3. What observations do you make after a few minutes?
4. Observation, explanation and conclusion.
5. After a few minutes, the ink or dye spread throughout the water in the beaker.
6. The ink pr dye spread from the region where it was highly concentrated to region in water where it was in low concentratio.

• Perfume smell spreads across a room: particles move from high to low concentration — that is diffusion.

What you do / what happens: 1. Place the scented flower in a corner of the classroom.

2. Remove the stopper of the perfume, hold it a few centimetres away from your friend’s nose.
3. Observation, explanation and conclusion.
4. After a few seconds, you and your classmates will be able to smell the scent of the flower or perfume. This is due to diffusion. The scent of the flower and perfume molecules diffuse the air to their nose.
5. Molecules in the scent of flower or perfume moved from the region of high concentratio and spread evenly towards the region of low concentratio.
6. Diffusion in gases also makes it possible for us to smell things, for example, flower, food being cooked and also foul smells.
You may use simple materials such as: A bottle of perfume of scented flowers..

PAGE 5: DIFFUSION

Grade 8 · Integrated Science · Topic 2.2: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell

▸ Today’s idea

• DIFFUSION — read, see the example, then do Your turn.

▸ Learn

Today we study: DIFFUSION.

Roles of diffusion in Living things. Plants absorb minerals salts from soil through diffusion.

• Nutrients such as glucose and amino acids move from the small intestines into bloodstream of animals by diffusion.
• Cells and unicellular organisms such as amoeba get rid of waste substance through diffusion.
• Gaseous exchange is the process through which gases are transferred across cell membrane to either enter or leave the blood. This process is done by diffusion in human beings in the alveoli in lungs. Oxygen gas moves from alveoli where is it is highly concentrated to the blood capillaries where it is lowly concentrated.
• On the other hand, carbon (IV) oxide moves from the capillaries where it is highly concentrated into the alveoli where it is lowly concentrated to be exhaled out.

▸ Worked example

• Perfume smell spreads across a room: particles move from high to low concentration — that is diffusion.
• Sugar in tea spreads without stirring until the tea tastes even — diffusion in a liquid.

▸ Your turn

PAGE 6: DIFFUSION

Grade 8 · Integrated Science · Topic 2.2: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell

▸ Today’s idea

• DIFFUSION — read, see the example, then do Your turn.

▸ Learn

Today we study: DIFFUSION.

Factors that affect the rate of diffusion. Concentratio gradient-molecules move from region of high concentratio to that of low concentratio. The greater the difference in concentratio between high and low regions, the faster the rate of diffusion.

• Temperature-high temperature increases energy and therefore faster movement of molecules. This increases the rate of diffusion.
• Mass of particles- heavy particles move slowly hence slower rate of diffusion. Light particles on the other hand move fast hence faster rate of diffusion.
• Diffusion distance- rate of diffusion depends on distance that particles have to travel in order to be evenly distributed within available space.

▸ Worked example

• Perfume smell spreads across a room: particles move from high to low concentration — that is diffusion.
• Sugar in tea spreads without stirring until the tea tastes even — diffusion in a liquid.

▸ Your turn

Capillary tube. A thread.

PAGE 11: THE CELL MEMBRANE

Grade 8 · Integrated Science · Topic 2.2: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell

▸ Today’s idea

• The cell membrane — read, see the example, then do Your turn.

▸ Learn

Today we study: The cell membrane.

Observation and explanation. The concentratio of water outside the visking tubing is higher than the concentratio of water inside the visking tubing.

• Water moves in through the pores in the semi-permeable membrane of the Visking tubing by osmosis because of the differences in concentratio inside and outside the visking tubing.
• Osmosis is the random movement of water (solvent) molecules from where they are more to where they are less through a semi-permeable membrane.
• Osmosis can also be defined as the random movement of water (solvent) molecules from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution through a semi-permeable membrane until the concentratio on each side is equal.

▸ Worked example

• Water moves from where it is more (dilute solution) to where it is less (concentrated solution) across a membrane.
• Kenya link: roots take in water from soil partly by osmosis.

▸ Your turn

PAGE 17: OSMOSIS IN ANIMALS

Grade 8 · Integrated Science · Topic 2.2: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell

▸ Today’s idea

• Osmosis in animals — read, see the example, then do Your turn.

▸ Learn

Today we study: Osmosis in animals.

Absorption of water in the human body. Excretion-this is the removal of waste products from the body. Urine is the main product through which excess water is excreted from the body. Kidneys filter urine to control the amount of water lost. This happens through osmosis. Similarities and difference between osmosis and diffusion.

• Similarities.
• Both are mean to equalize concentratio of two solutions.
• Both are passive transport processes, i.e., they do not require any energy to occur.
• In both, particles move from an area of higher concentratio to an area of low concentratio.
• Differences.
• Osmosis happens in liquid medium while diffusion happens in liquids, gases and even solids.

▸ Worked example

• Water moves from where it is more (dilute solution) to where it is less (concentrated solution) across a membrane.
• Kenya link: roots take in water from soil partly by osmosis.

• In osmosis there is only one way for particles to flow while in diffusion particles can flow in any direction.
